Marathon Petroleum fell 2.14% today after oil prices tumbled back below $100 per barrel on Monday, driven by Trump's openness to diplomacy with Iran and traders' hopes for a recovery in Saudi Arabian shipments. For a refiner like MPC, lower oil prices directly squeeze profit margins — the company buys crude at the wholesale price and sells refined products (gasoline, diesel) at retail rates, so when crude falls faster than refined products do, that spread narrows and cuts earnings potential.

The broader picture is complicated, though. While oil fell sharply today, US refineries are running at 96.8% capacity and gasoline and diesel inventories remain relatively lean, which normally supports prices for refined products. The real headwind appears to be uncertainty: geopolitical tensions around Iran, the Saudi pipeline shutdown, and conflicting signals about whether supplies will actually recover are creating volatility that weighs on the sector even as underlying demand remains solid.
